tax_name: None at federal level (state and local retail sales and use taxes only)
legal_ref: No federal VAT/GST statute; general sales taxes are imposed by states and localities (cf. IRC s.164 deduction for state and local general sales taxes)
quote: "State and local general sales taxes ... A general sales tax is a tax imposed at one rate on retail sales of a broad range of items." — IRS treats general sales taxes as state/local taxes (deductible federally); there is no federal VAT. CRS R41708: "The United States is the only member [of the OECD] without a VAT."
source_title: IRS Topic no. 503, Deductible taxes (irs.gov); supplementary: CRS Report R41708 'Value-Added Tax (VAT) as a Revenue Option: A Primer' (2011), read via everycrsreport.com mirror because congress.gov/crsreports.congress.gov served a bot challenge
notes: No national VAT or GST. 45 states plus DC levy state general sales/use taxes (Alaska, Delaware, Montana, New Hampshire and Oregon have no statewide sales tax; Alaska allows local sales taxes); many counties/cities add local sales taxes. Rates, bases and economic-nexus thresholds (post-Wayfair, 2018) vary by state. Federal excise taxes exist on specific goods only. GAO-08-566 (gao.gov) frames a VAT as a proposal under US tax-reform debate ('proposals for a national consumption tax').
unverified: Official statement 'the US has no federal VAT' taken from CRS R41708 via a non-government mirror (everycrsreport.com); congress.gov and gao.gov full texts were behind bot protection
List of states without statewide sales tax is general knowledge, not fetched from an official source
